questions.question: How many days of annual leave do full-time employees get per year?
questions.answer: According to the Leave Policy v2 (2. Annual leave): “Full-time employees accrue 16 days of annual leave per calendar year, credited each pay period in equal parts. Part-time employees accrue pro rata.” [1]
questions.expected: 16 days (Leave Policy v2, which supersedes v1's 12 days).

questions.question: How much vacation do I get?
questions.answer: According to the Leave Policy v2 (2. Annual leave): “Full-time employees accrue 16 days of annual leave per calendar year, credited each pay period in equal parts. Part-time employees accrue pro rata.” [1]
questions.expected: 16 days of annual leave per calendar year.

questions.question: How many sick days do employees get a year?
questions.answer: According to the Leave Policy v2 (3. Sick leave): “Employees receive 8 days of sick leave per year. A doctor's note is required for absences of three or more consecutive days.” [1]
questions.expected: 8 days of sick leave per year.

questions.question: How many unused leave days can I carry into next year, and when do they expire?
questions.answer: According to the Leave Policy v2 (4. Carry forward): “Up to 8 unused annual leave days may be carried into the next calendar year. Carried days must be used by March 31 or they lapse.” [1]
questions.expected: Up to 8 days; they must be used by March 31.

questions.question: Who needs to approve leave of more than ten consecutive working days?
questions.answer: According to the Leave Policy v2 (5. Approval): “Leave of more than ten consecutive working days also needs the department head's approval. Managers should respond to requests within two working days.” [1]
questions.expected: The direct manager and also the department head.

questions.question: How long before a scheduled release does the deploy freeze start?
questions.answer: According to the Production Deploy Runbook (1. When to deploy): “A deploy freeze starts 72 hours before every scheduled release and during declared incidents. Freeze exceptions need the on-call manager's approval in #deploys.” [1]
questions.expected: 72 hours (the deprecated 2023 runbook said 36 hours).

questions.question: How long after a deploy can I use the one-click rollback?
questions.answer: According to the Production Deploy Runbook (4. Rollback window): “A deploy can be rolled back with a single click in the deploy console for 45 minutes after full rollout completes. After that window, rollback requires a new deploy of the previous version following the Rollback Procedure.” [1]
questions.expected: 45 minutes after full rollout completes (2023 runbook said 10 minutes).

questions.question: How many approving reviews does a change to a production repository need?
questions.answer: According to the Code Review Guidelines: “Every change to a production repository needs 2 approving review(s) from someone other than the author before merge, plus a green CI pipeline. Reviews should be returned within one working day; if you cannot review in time, say so and suggest someone else.” [1]
questions.expected: 2 approving reviews from someone other than the author, plus green CI.

questions.question: How long does the canary stage run and how much traffic does it get?
questions.answer:
According to the Production Deploy Runbook (3. Rollout): “Deploys go through the canary stage (5 percent of traffic) for ten minutes, then to full rollout. Watch the error rate and p95 latency dashboards during the canary.” [1]

Also relevant, from the Database Migration Runbook: “Take a snapshot immediately before running the migration and verify that the snapshot is restorable in staging first.” [2]
questions.expected: Ten minutes at 5 percent of traffic.

questions.question: How many weeks of paid leave do secondary caregivers get?
questions.answer:
According to the Parental Leave Policy (Secondary caregiver leave): “Fathers and secondary caregivers receive 12 weeks of fully paid leave, to be taken within six months of the birth or adoption.” [1]

Upcoming change: the Parental Leave Policy (2027 revision) takes effect on 2027-01-01 and says: “Following the 2026 benefits review, secondary caregiver leave increases from 12 weeks to 26 weeks fully paid for births and adoptions on or after 2027-01-01.” [2] Until then the rule above applies.
questions.expected: 12 weeks today; 26 weeks for births/adoptions on or after 2027-01-01.

questions.question: My partner is due in March 2027. How much paid leave will I get as the secondary caregiver?
questions.answer:
According to the Parental Leave Policy (Secondary caregiver leave): “Fathers and secondary caregivers receive 12 weeks of fully paid leave, to be taken within six months of the birth or adoption.” [1]

Upcoming change: the Parental Leave Policy (2027 revision) takes effect on 2027-01-01 and says: “Following the 2026 benefits review, secondary caregiver leave increases from 12 weeks to 26 weeks fully paid for births and adoptions on or after 2027-01-01.” [2] Until then the rule above applies.
questions.expected: 26 weeks fully paid (2027 revision applies to births on or after 2027-01-01).

questions.question: How much leave does a birth parent get?
questions.answer:
According to the Parental Leave Policy (Birth parent leave): “Birth parents receive 16 weeks of fully paid leave, which runs concurrently with any FMLA entitlement. Up to four weeks may be taken before the expected due date.” [1]

Upcoming change: the Parental Leave Policy (2027 revision) takes effect on 2027-01-01 and says: “Birth parent leave is unchanged at 16 weeks.” [2] Until then the rule above applies.
questions.expected: 16 weeks of fully paid leave.

questions.question: What is the maximum hotel room rate per night in San Francisco?
questions.answer:
According to the Travel Policy (4. Limits > 4.2 Hotels and daily spending limits): “Hotel room rates, excluding taxes, are capped per night by city tier:

City tier | Maximum room rate per night

City tier: Tier 1 | Maximum room rate per night: $275

City tier: Tier 2 | Maximum room rate per night: $200

City tier: Tier 3 | Maximum room rate per night: $150” [1]

Also relevant, from the Travel Policy (3. City tiers): “Tier 1: New York, San Francisco, Boston” [2]
questions.expected: $275 (San Francisco is Tier 1).

questions.question: What's the nightly hotel cap when I travel to Austin?
questions.answer:
According to the Travel Policy (4. Limits > 4.2 Hotels and daily spending limits): “Hotel room rates, excluding taxes, are capped per night by city tier:

City tier | Maximum room rate per night

City tier: Tier 1 | Maximum room rate per night: $275

City tier: Tier 2 | Maximum room rate per night: $200

City tier: Tier 3 | Maximum room rate per night: $150” [1]
questions.expected: $150: Austin is not listed, so it falls in Tier 3.

questions.question: What is the maximum fare for a one-way domestic flight?
questions.answer: According to the Travel Policy (4. Limits > 4.1 Flights): “The maximum fare for a one-way domestic flight is $450 unless the trip is booked less than 48 hours before departure for an incident response, in which case the on-call manager may approve a higher fare in VoyageHub.” [1]
questions.expected: $450, unless booked under 48 hours before departure for incident response.

questions.question: What is the daily per diem for an L3 employee travelling to Chicago?
questions.answer:
According to the Per-Diem Table: “grade: L3 | city tier: 2 | example cities: Chicago, Seattle, Los Angeles, Washington DC | per diem usd: 75” [1]

Also relevant, from the Travel Policy (4. Limits > 4.2 Hotels and daily spending limits): “Daily per-diem allowances by grade and tier are published in the Per-Diem Table maintained by Finance.” [2]
questions.expected: $75 (Chicago is tier 2).

questions.question: Per diem for grade L2 in Boise?
questions.answer: According to the Per-Diem Table: “grade: L2 | city tier: 3 | example cities: Omaha, Tulsa, Boise, Albuquerque, Des Moines | per diem usd: 50” [1]

questions.question: Do I need to file an expense claim to get my per diem?
questions.answer: According to the Expense Policy (3. Travel limits): “Flight, hotel and per-diem limits for business travel are defined in section 4.2 of the Travel Policy. This document does not restate them; Finance will reject a travel claim that exceeds those limits unless an exception was recorded in VoyageHub.” [1]
questions.expected: No. Per diem is paid in advance when the trip is booked in VoyageHub; no claim is needed.

questions.question: Who has to approve an expense claim of $4,000?
questions.answer: According to the Expense Policy (4. Approval thresholds): “Claims above $2,500 require approval from a Vice President in addition to your manager, except travel that was booked through VoyageHub, which is pre-approved at booking time and needs only manager sign-off at claim time.” [1]
questions.expected: A Vice President, in addition to the direct manager (unless it is VoyageHub-booked travel).

questions.question: I booked a $3,200 trip through VoyageHub. Does the claim need VP approval?
questions.answer:
According to the VoyageHub Booking Guide: “Receipts for hotel stays are attached in VoyageHub, not in the expense system, so travel booked in VoyageHub does not need a separate expense claim or VP approval.” [1]

Also relevant, from the Reimbursement SLA: “Per-diem allowances are paid in advance when the trip is booked in VoyageHub; no claim is needed for them.” [2]
questions.expected: No: VoyageHub travel is pre-approved at booking and needs only manager sign-off (the approval matrix alone would suggest VP).

questions.question: How long does Finance take to process an approved expense claim?
questions.answer: According to the Reimbursement SLA: “Finance processes an approved expense claim within 5 business days of the final approval and pays it with the next payroll run. Claims returned for missing receipts restart the clock when resubmitted.” [1]
questions.expected: Within 5 business days of final approval, paid with the next payroll run.

questions.question: What's the deadline to submit an expense claim?
questions.answer: According to the Expense Policy (1. Principles): “Claim only what you spent, attach a receipt, and submit within 30 days of the expense.” [1]
questions.expected: Within 30 days of the expense.

questions.question: How much is the employee referral bonus?
questions.answer: According to the Employee Referral Policy: “If your referral is hired into a full-time role and completes 90 days of employment, you receive a referral bonus of $3,000 with the next payroll.” [1]
questions.expected: $3,000 once the hire completes 90 days (half for intern/contract roles).

questions.question: How long is the probation period for new hires?
questions.answer: According to the Introductory Period Policy: “New hires serve an introductory period, also called probation, of 6 months from their start date. Employment remains at will throughout; the introductory period sets expectations for feedback, not a contract term.” [1]
questions.expected: 6 months (the 'introductory period').

questions.question: How much notice should I give if I resign?
questions.answer: According to the Resignation Notice and Exit Process: “When resigning, employees are asked to give 4 weeks' notice so that work can be handed over; during the introductory period one week is sufficient. Managers may release an employee earlier, in which case the notice period is paid out.” [1]
questions.expected: 4 weeks; one week during the introductory period.

questions.question: How many days per week can I work from home?
questions.answer: According to the Remote Work Policy (Eligibility): “Employees past the introductory period may work remotely up to 2 days per week by default. Teams that run physical hardware labs set their own in-office days; check with your manager.” [1]
questions.expected: Up to 2 days per week by default, after the introductory period.

questions.question: Can I work remotely from Canada for a month?
questions.answer: According to the Remote Work Policy (Working from another state): “Working from outside the United States is not supported.” [1]
questions.expected: No. Working from outside the United States is not supported.

questions.question: How much can I claim for home office equipment?
questions.answer: According to the Remote Work Policy (Equipment): “A one-time home office allowance of $1,000 is available after the introductory period. Claim it under the WFH Equipment Policy.” [1]
questions.expected: Up to $1,000 once, after the introductory period.

questions.question: Who approves a laptop replacement?
questions.answer: According to the Laptop and Hardware Policy (2. Replacement): “Approval for a replacement comes from the employee's team engineering manager; IT does not approve replacements itself. Once approved, IT fulfils the request within 3 business days in Austin and Denver, and ships to remote employees within a further two days.” [1]
questions.expected: The employee's team engineering manager (not IT).

questions.question: How often are company laptops refreshed?
questions.answer:
According to the Laptop and Hardware Policy (2. Replacement): “Laptops are refreshed after 3 years. Early replacement for damage, theft or performance problems is requested through the IT portal.” [1]

Also relevant, from the Laptop and Hardware Policy (1. Standard issue): “Every employee receives a company laptop on day one.” [2]
questions.expected: Every 3 years.

questions.question: How many VPN sessions can I have open at once?
questions.answer: According to the VPN Guide: “You may hold at most 2 concurrent VPN sessions; a further device will be refused.” [1]
questions.expected: At most 2 concurrent sessions.

questions.question: What is the minimum password length?
questions.answer: According to the Password and Authentication Policy: “Passwords must be at least 16 characters long. Length matters more than symbols; passphrases are encouraged.” [1]
questions.expected: 16 characters.

questions.question: How quickly must a SEV2 page be acknowledged?
questions.answer:
According to the SEV Definitions: “SEV2: Major degradation or a single large customer down. Acknowledge within 45 minutes. Incident channel required. Post-incident review required.” [1]

Also relevant, from the SEV Definitions: “SEV1: Customer-facing outage, data loss, or robot safety fault. Acknowledge within 15 minutes. Incident commander required. Status page update required. Post-incident review required.” [2]
questions.expected: Within 45 minutes.

questions.question: If the primary on-call doesn't acknowledge a page, when is the secondary paged?
questions.answer: According to the On-Call Runbook (6. Escalation): “If the primary on-call does not acknowledge a page within 15 minutes, the paging tool pages the secondary automatically. If the secondary also fails to acknowledge within another 15 minutes, the page goes to the team's engineering manager.” [1]
questions.expected: After 15 minutes, automatically.

questions.question: I'm on an active SEV1 and need help right now. How do I reach the secondary?
questions.answer:
According to the On-Call Runbook (6. Escalation): “An engineer who needs help on an active SEV1 should not wait for the timers: call the secondary directly through the incident phone bridge on extension 304, which rings the secondary's phone and the manager's phone at the same time. Never escalate by Slack message alone during a SEV1; Slack is not a paging channel.” [1]

Also relevant, from the On-Call Runbook (3. Being reachable): “While on call, keep your phone charged and on loud, keep the paging app installed and logged in, and stay within reach of a laptop with VPN access.” [2]
questions.expected: Call through the incident phone bridge on extension 304; don't wait for timers or use Slack alone.

questions.question: What is the RTO for the payments service?
questions.answer: According to the Disaster Recovery Runbook (1. Objectives): “Service: Payments service | RTO: 4 hours | RPO: 5 minutes” [1]
questions.expected: 4 hours.

questions.question: What is the recovery point objective for the orders database?
questions.answer:
According to the Disaster Recovery Runbook (1. Objectives): “Service: Orders database | RTO: 6 hours | RPO: 30 minutes” [1]

Also relevant, from the Disaster Recovery Runbook (2. Backups): “Databases are backed up continuously to a second region with point-in-time recovery.” [2]
questions.expected: 30 minutes.

questions.question: What does RTO stand for?
questions.answer: According to the Glossary: “RTO: Recovery Time Objective. The maximum acceptable time to restore a service after a disaster. Not to be confused with return-to-office arrangements, which are covered by the Remote Work Policy.” [1]
questions.expected: Recovery Time Objective (not return-to-office).

questions.question: What time do production database migrations run?
questions.answer: According to the Database Migration Runbook: “Schema migrations on production databases run in the maintenance window starting at 03:00 Central Time. Every migration must be reversible or must ship with a documented restore path.” [1]
questions.expected: In the maintenance window starting at 03:00 Central Time.

questions.expected: 1700 Platte Street.

questions.question: How much is the on-call stipend?
questions.answer: According to the On-Call Runbook (2. Rotations): “An on-call stipend of $500 per week is paid for the primary role and half that for the secondary role.” [1]
questions.expected: $500 per week for primary, half that for secondary.

questions.question: How long are application logs kept?
questions.answer:
According to the Data Retention Policy: “Application logs are retained for 365 days and then deleted.” [1]

Also relevant, from the Handbook Index (Sections): “Documents marked deprecated are kept for history and must not be followed.” [2]
questions.expected: 365 days.

questions.question: How many quotes do I need for a $50,000 purchase?

According to the Procurement Policy: “Three quotes are needed above $40,000.” [1]

Also relevant, from the Procurement Policy: “Purchases above $10,000 go through Procurement with a purchase order.” [2]
questions.expected: Three quotes (required above $40,000).

questions.question: What is my annual training and conference budget?
questions.answer: According to the Training and Conference Policy: “Each employee has an annual budget of $3,000 for conferences, courses, certifications and books. Your direct manager approves spend within the budget; anything above it is a department head decision.” [1]
questions.expected: $3,000 per year.

questions.question: How many paid holidays does the company observe each year?
questions.answer: According to the Working Hours and Holidays: “The company observes 11 paid holidays per year; the dated list is in the Holiday Calendar CSV. Optional floating holidays: two per year, chosen by the employee.” [1]
questions.expected: 11 paid holidays, plus two optional floating holidays.

questions.question: Who approves service credits for customers after an outage?
questions.answer: According to the Customer Support Escalation (Customer credits): “Service credits for outages are approved by the Head of Product and processed by Finance.” [1]
questions.expected: The Head of Product; Finance processes them.

questions.question: Who is allowed to publish status page updates?
questions.answer: According to the Customer Support Escalation (Status page): “Only the Support lead and the incident commander may publish status page updates. Engineers draft the wording in the incident channel; Support publishes it.” [1]
questions.expected: Only the Support lead and the incident commander.

questions.question: What is the monthly limit on a corporate card?
questions.answer: According to the Corporate Card Policy: “The monthly limit is $10,000. Every transaction needs a receipt uploaded within seven days.” [1]

questions.question: I clicked a link in a phishing email. What should I do?
questions.answer: According to the Security Incident Reporting: “If you suspect a security incident, such as a phishing email you clicked, a lost device, or unexpected access to a system, report it immediately to security@northgate.example and post in #security-incidents.” [1]
questions.expected: Report immediately to security@northgate.example and post in #security-incidents; don't investigate yourself.

questions.question: What is needed before onboarding a new vendor that will handle customer data?
questions.answer: According to the Vendor Policy: “New vendors are onboarded by Finance and Legal: a signed agreement, a W-9, and for vendors handling customer data, a security assessment by the Security team. Robot hardware components come from the approved vendor list maintained by the Robotics Firmware team and Procurement; substitutions need an engineering change note.” [1]
questions.expected: Signed agreement, W-9, and a security assessment by the Security team.

questions.question: How long can hardware-in-the-loop tests take in CI?
questions.answer: According to the CI Pipeline Guide: “Firmware repositories additionally run hardware-in-the-loop tests on the lab bench pool, which are queued and may take up to 40 minutes. Flaky tests are quarantined with a ticket, never retried silently.” [1]
questions.expected: Up to 40 minutes (queued on the lab bench pool).

questions.question: What do I need to wear in the hardware lab?
questions.answer: According to the Lab Safety Rules: “Closed shoes and safety glasses in the hardware lab at all times. Robot arms under test run inside the marked cells with the light curtain active; never reach into a cell while the arm is powered.” [1]
questions.expected: Closed shoes and safety glasses.
